subject: Business Models
title: Theranos: Fake It Till You Break It
description: One-minute skill: Theranos: Fake It Till You Break It.

hook.text: Theranos claimed to run 200+ blood tests from a single finger prick. The technology never worked.

buildup.text: Elizabeth Holmes raised $700 million from investors who never saw the technology demonstrated independently.

discovery.text: Theranos secretly ran most tests on standard machines from Siemens, diluting finger-prick blood to make it work.

twist.text: The deception endangered patients. Inaccurate blood tests led to wrong diagnoses and dangerous medical decisions.

climax.text: Holmes was convicted of fraud and sentenced to 11 years. The 'fake it till you make it' ethos met legal reality.

punchline.text: $700M raised, tech never worked, 11 years in prison. Some fakes never make it.

quiz.question: What was Theranos actually doing with blood tests?
options: Secretly running tests on standard machines with diluted samples

details.summary: Theranos claimed its proprietary technology could run hundreds of blood tests from a single finger prick. The technology never worked as promised, but founder Elizabeth Holmes raised over 700 million dollars from investors by fabricating demonstrations and suppressing internal dissent.
details.whyItMatters: Theranos is the ultimate cautionary tale of fake-it-till-you-make-it culture taken to criminal extremes. It endangered patients, destroyed investor capital, and showed how charisma and secrecy can mask fundamental product failure.
takeaways: The core blood-testing technology never actually worked as demonstrated
Secrecy and intimidation prevented whistleblowers from exposing the fraud
Holmes was convicted of fraud after destroying 700 million in investor capital

faq.question: How did Theranos deceive investors for so long?
faq.answer: Extreme secrecy prevented due diligence. Celebrity board members lent credibility. Staged demonstrations used commercial machines secretly. NDAs and legal threats silenced employees. Holmes's charismatic storytelling convinced investors to trust the vision over evidence.

faq.question: What were the consequences of Theranos's deception?
faq.answer: Patients received inaccurate blood test results potentially affecting medical decisions. Over 700 million in investor capital was destroyed. Elizabeth Holmes was convicted of four counts of fraud and sentenced to over 11 years in prison.
